subject_constraints: allow rustic barn architecture, chickens, feed scoop, nesting-box doors and latches, worn 1930s-era physics-book materials, sealed box constructions, simplified radioactive atom motifs, mechanically linked detector-trigger-poison apparatus, cat silhouettes, branching probability forms, overlapping alive/dead visual states, wave-like interference shapes and restrained early-physics diagram vocabulary; quantum ambiguity should be expressed through layered spatial overlap rather than multiple unrelated art styles

hero_rendering_in_world: render the protagonist as a layered cut-card figure with graphite-defined facial features, preserving his recognizable hair silhouette, beard shape and overalls silhouette; use warm barn-colored paper layers in ordinary scenes and allow only subtle cool edge echoes when he visually enters the quantum explanation
negative_constraints: no photorealism, no glossy 3D CGI, no anime or manga styling, no neon cyberpunk laboratory, no generic sci-fi holograms, no excessive glow, no literal gore or distressed animal imagery, no beat-by-beat medium switching, no oversized empty subtitle void, and no visible text, letters, numbers, labels, captions, equations or UI inside generated world imagery
reason: A new surreal shadow-box collage directly connects the episode's closed nesting-box trigger to Schrödinger's sealed-box thought experiment: physical layers can conceal, reveal and simultaneously overlap alternate states while remaining visually intuitive. The warm cardboard barn world can transition coherently into deep layered quantum compartments without changing the primary medium. Creating a new style also satisfies the operator directive and increases between-episode diversity; recent episodes already used painted-storybook, historical-engraving and ink-wash families, so repeating those textures would incur a strong recent-usage penalty.
